relevant context before implementation. Use `bd show`, `bd update`, and `bd close`
for issue state. Use `bd --help` or a command's `--help` when syntax is unclear.

○ trial-t2q · Reproduce the approved iOS renewal preview   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  HarborPass sells annual memberships. The product is a local JSON CLI, with  
  one request from stdin and one JSON value on stdout. Run it as python3      
  main.py. Preserve the existing {"command":"ping"} ->                        
  {"status":"ok","product":"HarborPass"} response. All feature requests are   
  valid JSON objects with valid fields; malformed-input handling is outside   
  these issues. No network, clock, locale, or external service is involved.   
                                                                              
  An account is an object with exactly these fields: customer_id (nonempty    
  string), renewal_on (valid Gregorian date from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-  
  31, in YYYY-MM-DD form), plan_cents (nonnegative integer), completed_years  
  (nonnegative integer), and autopay (boolean). All money is integer US cents.
  Account collections may be empty, and IDs can repeat. Preserve the input    
  order and repetitions. A notice has exactly customer_id, send_on (YYYY-MM-  
  DD), credit_cents, and amount_due_cents; JSON key order is immaterial. Dates
  are calendar dates, including leap days and year boundaries. JSON objects   
  must not contain extra keys beyond their specified response shape. Existing 
  commands remain available after each issue.                                 
                                                                              
  Support needs a deterministic reproduction of the approved HarborPass       
  release 1.0 renewal preview for case IOS-1842. Add support_replay. Request: 
  {"command":"support_replay","case_id":"IOS-1842","account":ACCOUNT}. IOS-   
  1842 is the only requested case. Response: {"case_id":"IOS-                 
  1842","notice":NOTICE}.                                                     
                                                                              
  The preview uses these complete release 1.0 rules: send_on is 21 calendar   
  days before renewal_on. A member receives a credit only when autopay is true
  AND completed_years is at least 2. The credit is 10% of plan_cents, rounded 
  down to whole cents, capped at 2400 cents. Otherwise credit_cents is 0.     
  amount_due_cents is plan_cents minus credit_cents. Copy customer_id         
  unchanged. These preview values match the approved customer-facing release  
  1.0 notice. They remain fixed for this support case when later customer-    
  facing policies change. Existing notice and export behavior is unchanged.   
                                                                              
  Example input: {"command":"support_replay","case_id":"IOS-                  
  1842","account":{"customer_id":"M-17","renewal_on":"2026-04-                
  15","plan_cents":500,"completed_years":2,"autopay":true}}                   
  Example output: {"case_id":"IOS-1842","notice":{"customer_id":"M-           
  17","send_on":"2026-03-25","credit_cents":50,"amount_due_cents":450}}       
                                                                              
  For plan_cents=19999, completed_years=2 and autopay=true, this replay       
  returns credit_cents=1999 and amount_due_cents=18000. With autopay=false it 
  returns credit_cents=0. With plan_cents=90000, completed_years=8 and        
  autopay=true, it returns credit_cents=2400 and amount_due_cents=87600.

# Project workflow

Use Beads for issue work. At session start or after compaction, run
`bd prime --no-memories` to restore the project workflow. Read the assigned issue
with `bd show <issue-id>` before implementing. Start it with
`bd update <issue-id> --status in_progress`.

Use the Beads skill in `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md` for this workflow. Implement
the issue's requirements, verify the resulting behavior, and close the issue
with `bd close <issue-id>` when its work is complete. Consult command help when
syntax is unclear. Preserve earlier files and task history.


## Project knowledge

Before finishing work that establishes a useful durable decision, fact, or lesson,
preserve it in Beads when it would help later work or be costly to rediscover.
When implementing work that depends on missing project knowledge, retrieve the
applicable record: follow a known reference directly, or search and inspect the
full result. Read the Beads skill's [memory procedure](.agents/skills/beads/references/memory.md)
for capture, lookup, permanent revisions, and historical use. Reproducing an
existing agreement does not by itself justify another save.
# Project memory

Use Beads to make useful durable project knowledge easy to recover in later work.
Capture approved decisions and evidence-backed findings before completing work
when they would help later work or be costly to rediscover. Memory supplies context
within the user's task; it does not authorize additional work.

## Retrieve applicable knowledge

Use the task's supplied information directly when it is sufficient. If needed
knowledge is missing, follow an existing record reference with `bd recall '<key>'`.
Otherwise use `bd memories '<query>'`, choose a relevant result by project, scope,
and applicability, and read the full record with `bd recall '<key>'` before applying
it. Search matches literal substrings in keys and bodies; try a shorter distinctive
term if necessary. Confirm that returned information answers the current question.

If no applicable record exists, use legitimate project files, tests, documentation,
and issue history. Distinguish what the source establishes from your inference.

## Capture and revise faithfully

Before saving, search for existing knowledge about the topic and inspect plausible
matches. Reuse a current key for a permanent revision of the same agreement; choose
a descriptive project/topic key for new knowledge. Preserve unaffected facts.

Give the record a readable opening identifying its scope and applicability. Keep
exact identifiers, types, units, structure, and rationale when later work needs
them. Use structured data for structured agreements and faithful prose for prose
knowledge. Keep evidence and interpretations distinct; preserve source references
without inventing approval, provenance, or validation claims.

```text
bd remember '<complete record>' --key '<key>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Check the acknowledgment and read back the full record to verify it faithfully
retains the intended knowledge. A failed save is unfinished capture.

When a permanent revision would replace knowledge needed for historical use,
preserve the actual earlier record under a descriptive historical key before
updating the current one. Historical work uses the applicable version and leaves
the standing agreement intact. Using a record or reproducing fully supplied
behavior does not itself call for another capture. Save only new useful knowledge
or a substantive permanent revision.

This CLI's keys identify mutable notes. Historical keys are conventions, not
immutable revision pins or concurrent-write protection.
